subtitle: Lesson 8 · Classical Error Correction Review

steps.label: No unitary, no measurement, no combination can clone |ψ⟩
steps.sub: No process produces two independent copies while leaving the original intact

steps.label: It follows from linearity, not hardware limits
steps.sub: A machine that clones |0⟩ and |1⟩ correctly fails on (|0⟩+|1⟩)/√2

steps.label: It won't be engineered away with better qubits
steps.sub: This is a foundational mathematical result

steps.label: It only forbids copying an unknown state
steps.sub: Preparing many copies of a known state, like |0⟩, is always fine

steps.label: Encoding b as bbb assumes copying is free and perfect
steps.sub: A classical bit can be read and copied without disturbing it

steps.label: No-cloning removes that assumption entirely for qubits
steps.sub: You cannot turn |ψ⟩ into |ψ⟩|ψ⟩|ψ⟩ to vote over later

steps.label: This is precisely why 'just repeat the qubit' fails
steps.sub: At the most basic step — before you even get to measuring it

eyebrow: How quantum codes get redundancy anyway

steps.label: Encode 1 logical qubit into 3 physical qubits via entanglement
steps.sub: CNOTs build this circuit explicitly, starting next chapter

steps.label: No single physical qubit holds a copy of the logical state
steps.sub: The information is distributed across correlations between qubits

steps.label: You can measure the correlations, not the logical state
steps.sub: Stabilizer/syndrome measurements reveal only 'did an error happen'

steps.label: Never 'what is α and β' — that stays protected
steps.sub: This is the move that gets around no-cloning without breaking it
